generalfeedback: Since the degree of the numerator is greater than the degree of the denominator we need to use long division to get a simpler form to express \[{{CT:0}}.\] [[facts:alg_partial_fractions]] Using long division we get that \[{{CT:0}} = {{CT:2}} + {{CT:3}}\] Now, \[{{CT:2}} = {{CT:4}}{{CT:5}} + {{CT:6}}{{CT:7}}\] So, multiplying by {{CT:8}} both sides we get \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:9}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:10}} + {{CT:11}} \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:12}} \end{array}\] So, equating cefficients in {{CT:13}} we get that a system of equations that can be solved to get \(A = {{CT:14}}\) and \(B = {{CT:15}}\) Hence, \[{{CT:0}} = {{CT:16}}\] So, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int {{CT:16}} d{{CT:1}} \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:14}} \int {{CT:5}} d{{CT:1}} + {{CT:15}} \int {{CT:7}} d{{CT:1}} + \int ({{CT:3}}) d{{CT:1}} \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:17}} + {{CT:18}} + {{CT:19}}+c \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:20}}+c \end{array}\]
